issues.title: Hardcoded fallback JWT secret in two places
issues.detail: Both the middleware and token utility fall back to the string `'superSecret'` when `JWT_SECRET` is not set. If the environment variable is absent in production, every token is signed with a publicly known secret, letting anyone forge valid tokens.

issues.title: Race condition in uniqueness check
issues.detail: The two `findUnique` calls and the subsequent `create` are not wrapped in a transaction. Two concurrent registrations with the same email can both pass the check; one will fail with a raw Prisma unique-constraint error instead of the friendly 422.

issues.title: No email format validation
issues.detail: Any non-blank string is accepted as an email — there is no regex or format check. A user can register with `email: "x"` and receive a valid token.

group.note: Two independent pieces: the middleware that guards routes, and the utility that creates tokens.

children.detail: The `auth` object exports two `express-jwt` middleware instances: `required` (rejects requests without a valid token) and `optional` (allows unauthenticated requests but decodes the token if present). Both read the secret from `JWT_SECRET` with a hardcoded fallback.

issues.title: Fallback secret is the same string in both files
issues.detail: Both the middleware verifier and the token signer default to `'superSecret'`. If `JWT_SECRET` is unset, they agree on the same weak secret so everything works silently in production with a guessable key.

children.title: Token Extraction
children.sub: Reads the JWT string from the Authorization header, supporting both Token and Bearer schemes.
children.detail: `getTokenFromHeaders` splits the Authorization header on spaces. If the first word is `Token` or `Bearer` (case-sensitive), it returns the second word; otherwise null.

rows.title: Check scheme
rows.detail: Only `Token` or `Bearer` (case-sensitive) are accepted; anything else returns null.

children.title: Required Vs Optional
children.sub: Two express-jwt instances: one enforces token presence, the other permits anonymous access.
children.detail: Both use `HS256` and the same secret. `auth.required` rejects missing or invalid tokens with 401; `auth.optional` sets `credentialsRequired: false`, letting the request proceed unauthenticated.

issues.title: getCurrentUser crashes on a deleted user
issues.detail: If the user id from the JWT no longer exists in the database, `findUnique` returns null. The result is cast as `User` and `user.id` is accessed on the next line, causing an unhandled TypeError instead of a proper 404 or 401.

issues.title: Update skips uniqueness and validation
issues.detail: Unlike `createUser`, `updateUser` does not trim inputs, check for blank values, or call `checkUserUniqueness`. A user can set their email to another user's email; the Prisma unique constraint will throw a raw database error instead of a friendly 422.

issues.title: Truthy check prevents clearing bio or image
issues.detail: The spread pattern `...(bio ? { bio } : {})` skips falsy values including empty string. A user cannot clear their bio or image by sending an empty string — the field is simply left unchanged.

issues.detail: Neither the controller nor the service compares the authenticated user's id with the target username. A user can POST follow on their own profile, creating a self-referencing follower row.

issues.detail: `followUser` and `unfollowUser` call `prisma.user.update` without an existence check. Unlike `getProfile`, they have no guard, so a missing user triggers a raw Prisma error that the global handler turns into a 500.

issues.title: Each user gets a different tag list
issues.detail: The OR filter mixes demo tags with the caller's own tags but excludes all other real users' tags. Two logged-in users see different top-10 lists, and a tag popular across many non-demo users may never appear for anyone.

issues.title: Popularity count is scoped, not global
issues.detail: The orderBy articles._count only counts articles whose author matches the OR filter. A tag with 100 articles from real users and 1 from a demo user ranks as having 1 article for an anonymous caller.

issues.title: updatedAt never auto-updates
issues.detail: Both Article and Comment use `@default(now())` instead of Prisma’s `@updatedAt` directive. The article service manually sets `updatedAt: new Date()` on update, but any other update path — or a future comment-update feature — will leave a stale creation-time timestamp.
